label: rem:h3-markov-wenzl-weights-context
title: Scope, Borromean corollary, chirality, and notation for the H_3 Wenzl weights
html:
Scope — which trace, in which channel

This proposition concerns the Jones / Temperley–Lieb normalisation of the \mathrm{H}_3(q) Markov trace — the trace whose value on a braid closure is the Jones polynomial. Its defining feature is y_{(1^3)} \equiv 0: the Temperley–Lieb quotient annihilates the three-row partition. In the trace-convention registry this is convention D, with Ocneanu parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1).

The binding channel uses convention D as well, since the owner ruling of 2026-08-09 excised convention C. There is now one trace in the framework's compute, not two.

Convention C excised (owner ruling, 2026-08-09). Until then a second trace ran in the binding channel: the full-Hecke Ocneanu trace, convention C, z = 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}), with Wedderburn weights from the Wenzl Schur-principal specialisation and three-row weight y_{(1^3)}(q) \neq 0 for q \neq 1. It was pinned by rem:markov-axioms-primitive, which described its own z as "a stipulation of this definition, not a consequence of it".

It is gone because the selection turned out to be forced: lem:feynman-eigenbasis-decomposition already puts the row cap \ell(\lambda) \leq 2 in the mass channel's decomposition, giving y_{(1^3)} = 0, and markovWeights_eq_jones_of_threeRow_eq_zero (sorry-free) then makes z = q^3/(q^2+1) the unique faithful normalised Markov trace.

Not decided by experimental match, and the numbers say so. Switching the binding channel to D makes the aggregate worse — mean |{\rm err}| over \{{}^2H, ^3H, ^3He, ^4He, ^6Li, ^7Li\} moves 37.39\% \to 43.85\%. What it fixes is structural: under C the deuteron was unreachable, B_{\rm AME} = 2.2246 lying 30.4\% below the whole admissible band [2.9072, 5.1780] MeV; under D the band is [2.0507, 3.7978] and AME sits inside it. {}^2H itself improves +74.85\% \to +27.36\%.

The mass channel was already on D in production, so the m_e-scaled renderings of m_p and m_n are unchanged (verified: 938.27208943, 939.56542276).

Path A (ladder linear system) = Path B (Wenzl Schur) as a \mathbb{Z}-Laurent identity remains proven for C in the y_\lambda–\mathrm{tr}_M equivalence proof (docs/audits/2026-05-05-y-lambda-tr-m-equivalence-proof.md); that identity is about C and is now historical.

By contrast, the production mass channel uses convention D — the closed form of this proposition, entering as trM_borromean \to F_Bor \to canonical_mass.

The mass channel is convention D, and an earlier version of this note was wrong to say otherwise. The two blocks that define the mass channel already fix its fibre: lem:feynman-eigenbasis-decomposition carries the row cap \ell(\lambda) \leq 2 inside the index set of V^{\otimes n} \cong \bigoplus V_\lambda \otimes S_\lambda, and feynman-markov-identification carries it inside \mathrm{tr}_M itself, with closed-form weights that evaluate at N = 2, n = 3 to exactly the convention-D vector. So y_{(1^3)} = 0 is stated, not assumed, and D follows. Independently, the Ocneanu parameter determines the fibre dimension through z \cdot [N]_q = q^N, which is injective in N: convention D gives N = 2 exactly, while convention C gives N \approx 2.5995 — no integer fibre dimension at all. Convention C is a legitimate Markov trace on \mathrm{H}_3(q); it is simply not the trace of any fibre, so it cannot be the mass trace.

What remains is a definitional erratum, not a production defect: the z stipulated in rem:markov-axioms-primitive selects C, while that block and prop:categorical-mass-markov both name the Jones–Markov trace, which is D. The stipulated value 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) is the Temperley–Lieb loop reciprocal 1/\delta — correct for the TL generator e_i, but applied there to the Hecke generator \sigma_n; the value that lands on Jones under \sigma-stabilisation is z = q^3/(q^2+1). The registry channel mass records this resolution. Correcting the stipulation is tracked as an open item, and the separate question of whether the binding channel should also move to D is untouched by this proposition and remains open.

The two traces coincide at the symmetric point q = 1 (both give (\tfrac12,\tfrac14,0)) and diverge for q \neq 1: the convention-C weights at the substrate are (0.4154,\,0.2809,\,0.0227) against convention D's (0.5054,\,0.2473,\,0).

What writhe 0 does and does not buy. For \beta \in B_3 with writhe 0 and \pi(\beta) = \mathrm{id} both one-dimensional characters equal 1, so by the corollary below the trace depends on the weights only through y_{(2,1)}: the split between y_{(3)} and y_{(1^3)} is invisible, because normalisation \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1 already pins their sum. This is exactly why the chirality asymmetry discussed below is unobservable on such braids. It does not make two conventions agree. Two normalised Markov traces agree on such a braid precisely when they share y_{(2,1)} or when \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta) = 2, and \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} satisfies neither (y^{C}_{(2,1)} \neq 1/[2]_q^{2} = y^{D}_{(2,1)}):

  \mathrm{tr}^{D}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) - \mathrm{tr}^{C}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  \bigl(y^{D}_{(2,1)} - y^{C}_{(2,1)}\bigr)\bigl(-3h^4 - h^6\bigr)
  \;\approx\; 1.9554 \times 10^{-4},

exact as a rational function in q, and 195.8 ppm at the substrate. Consequently the closed forms below should be read as the convention-D (Jones-polynomial) weights, not as the convention-C y_\lambda used by the binding pipeline.

Immediate corollary — the Borromean closed form in one line

For any writhe-0 braid \beta \in B_3 with \pi(\beta) = \mathrm{id} \in S_3:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta)
  \;=\;
  1 + \frac{\chi^{(2,1)}(\beta) - 2}{[2]_q^{2}}.

The entire h-dependence of such traces is carried by the single standard-channel character; the Borromean closed form is this identity evaluated at \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 2 - 3h^4 - h^6.

Non-uniformity of the weights — chirality of the Jones trace

A bar-involution argument would suggest y_{(3)} = y_{(1^3)} (the transpose pair). It fails: the transpose symmetry \lambda \leftrightarrow \lambda^T is induced by the sign-twist automorphism \sigma_i \mapsto -q\,\sigma_i^{-1}, and the Jones-normalised Markov trace is not invariant under this automorphism — it is chiral, weighting the \sigma- and \sigma^{-1}-eigenchannels asymmetrically. The extreme expression of this asymmetry is y_{(1^3)} \equiv 0 against y_{(3)}(1) = 1/2.

At q = 1 the trace reduces to the cycle-counting trace \mathrm{tr}_M(w) = 2^{\,c(w) - n} on \mathbb{C}[S_3] (c(w) = number of cycles), and Schur orthogonality reproduces (\tfrac12, \tfrac14, 0) directly.

Notation note — y_\lambda, \mu_\lambda, \chi^\lambda, w_\lambda are distinct

Four \lambda-indexed scalars appear in the Hecke-algebra blocks of this paper. They are easy to conflate by symbol similarity but encode independent data:

  • y_\lambda(q) — Wenzl/Markov coefficient: appears in \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \cdot \chi^\lambda, normalised by \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \, d_\lambda = 1. This proposition gives the Jones/TL values (y_{(1^3)} \equiv 0), i.e. convention D; the full-Hecke Ocneanu trace (convention C) used by the binding pipeline has different y_\lambda at q \neq 1 (y_{(1^3)} \neq 0) — see the Scope note above.
  • \chi^\lambda(g) — character: trace of the V_\lambda-representation on a specific element g (e.g. a braid).
  • \mu_\lambda(q) — q-Laplacian eigenvalue on V_\lambda (prop:q-heat-kernel-peter-weyl): the heat-kernel decay rate, not a Markov-trace ingredient.
  • w_\lambda(q) = [n]_q! / H_q(\lambda)^2 — Plancherel measure (rem:symmetric-point-resolution-loss): normalised by \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(1) = 1 at q = 1 only — the q-deformed sum \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(q) is not 1 (0.987 at n = 3, 1.051 at n = 8, measured in docs/audits/scripts/wlambda_normalisation_census.py); at q = 1 it is non-uniform in a different pattern (\tfrac16, \tfrac23, \tfrac16 for n = 3) from the Wenzl weights of this proposition (\tfrac12, \tfrac14, 0).

Significance for the Borromean derivation

The 1/4 factor in h^4(\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})) = (-3) \cdot (1/4) = -3/4 is y_{(2,1)}(q = 1) = 1/[2]_q^2|_{q=1} from this proposition — and the identity y_{(2,1)}(q) = 1/[2]_q^2 holds exactly for all q, not only at the symmetric point. The Borromean h^4 separation into character coefficient \times Markov normalisation is therefore an exact structural fact, with the (h^2 + 4) denominator of the closed form being precisely [2]_q^2 = 1/y_{(2,1)}(q).

Correction note (scope). An earlier draft of the scope note above stated that the framework's mass and binding computations use the full-Hecke Ocneanu trace, and that the two traces coincide on writhe-0, \pi=\mathrm{id} braids, "which is why every physical mass prediction is insensitive to the distinction". Both parts were wrong. The production mass channel is on convention D, not C; and writhe 0 makes only the y_{(3)}–y_{(1^3)} split invisible, not y_{(2,1)}, so the two conventions differ on \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} — which is writhe 0 with \pi = \mathrm{id} — by 195.8 ppm exactly. The corrected statements are above; the trace-convention registry is now the machine-checked source of truth for which channel uses which trace.

Correction note. An earlier draft of this proposition claimed the q = 1 weights were uniform (y_\lambda(1) = 1/4 for all \lambda \vdash 3) via a bar-involution argument. That claim was wrong — caught in review — for the reason documented in the chirality section above: the Jones trace is not sign-twist invariant. The corrected weights (\tfrac12, \tfrac14, 0) are verified three ways: Schur orthogonality on the q = 1 cycle-counting trace, the exact q-dependent closed forms above, and canonical reproduction of the Borromean closed form at 30 digits.
